text.p: Supertyphoon Rosie, with 150 mph winds, is expected to pass east of Okinawa on its track to the north. Rosie is expected to head for southern Japan, and landfall should occur within 48 hours in eastern Kyushu or western Shikoku. The actual center may pass just between the two islands. Top winds at the time of expected landfall should be near 110 mph. This is a dangerous system. It poses an extreme risk to shipping, including in the port of Osaka, even if that region does not get a direct hit. Rosie may cause severe damage from heavy rain, flooding, coastal storm surge, winds, and mudslides in southern Japan.

Significant flooding has occurred over northeastern Europe the past several days. More rainfall over the weekend added to already severe flooding in eastern Germany and especially Poland, near the Oder River. The next storm system should pass mostly south of this region, not adding much rainfall to rivers. Property damage has been extensive in some locations, and crop losses are being reported. Cleanup may take weeks, but will be delayed by any additional storminess.

More rains are causing additional flooding problems in Bangladesh. Recent flooding, combined with new scattered monsoon rainfall, will add to flooding and may result in more property damage over the next few days.
